chunks: From him, from his father, from Hammad ibn Isa, from Ibrahim ibn Umar al-Yamani, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) who said:

Usury (riba) is of two types: a usury that is consumed and a usury that is not consumed. As for that which is consumed, it is your gift to a man when you seek from him a reward greater than it; that is the usury that is consumed.
And what you give in usury to increase within the wealth of people will not increase with Allah.
And as for that which is not consumed, it is that which Allah, Exalted and Mighty, forbade and threatened with the Fire.

key_terms.يُؤْكَلُ: Consumed (metaphorically used for hidden or effective interest)

ai.seo_question: What is the difference between consumed and unconsumed usury in Shia jurisprudence?
ai.summary: In this hadith from *Tahdhib al-Ahkam*, Imam al-Sadiq (AS) elucidates the nuanced classification of *riba* into 'consumed' (*mukal*) and 'non-consumed' (*ghayr mukal*), distinguishing between hidden interest disguised as gifts and the broader, severe prohibition carrying the threat of Hellfire. This distinction highlights the Shia scholarly emphasis on intent and economic subterfuge, linking the 'consumed' form directly to the Quranic verse in Surah Al-Baqarah regarding those who consume usury to increase wealth.
